# PyObject import fails after being moved from MOVED_IN_V2 to REMOVED_IN_V2

#### Description
I noticed that importing PyObject from pydantic or pydantic.types is failing after a recent change. It seems that PyObject was moved from the MOVED_IN_V2 dictionary to the REMOVED_IN_V2 set, but this breaks backward compatibility for code that depends on this import.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce
```python
from pydantic import PyObject

# OR

from pydantic.types import PyObject
```

#### Expected Results
The import should work as it did before, possibly with a deprecation warning.

#### Actual Results
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/path/to/pydantic/__init__.py", line 82, in __getattr__
    return getattr_migration('pydantic')(name)
  File "/path/to/pydantic/_migration.py", line 304, in wrapper
    raise AttributeError(f'module {module!r} has no attribute {name!r}')
AttributeError: module 'pydantic' has no attribute 'PyObject'
```

#### Versions
```
pydantic: 2.1.0
python: 3.10.16
```

This is breaking our codebase that relies on PyObject for dynamic imports. We were planning to migrate to ImportString but haven't completed that work yet.

Scope of this editing session: update the following production files and report the resulting local change for handover: pydantic/_migration.py. No full task validation has been performed in this session.
